audio_protocol: 32 separate source films. Seeded hash ordering of human annotated sound intervals lasting 60 ms to 2.6 s. One interval per film with category balancing. Same bounds supplied to each revision. Decode the selected channel PCM independently from the beginning, verify the physically cut WAV sample for sample against that slice, then let FFmpeg convert that bounded WAV. Require the same number of output samples and absolute error at most 1e-6 of full scale for every sample. Three configurations in order: original rate and channels, 16 kHz mono (transcription), 44.1 kHz stereo (separation). This is a signal fidelity test. No listener identified the events in this experiment.
controls_protocol: Float stereo inputs at six native sample rates and three target sample rates, with a single impulse just before the start, on the first retained sample, on the last retained sample or just after the interval. All controls fed into mono. Positive means strictly nonzero. Values are relative to digital full scale.
picture_protocol: 16 source films selected in seeded hash order. Choose a changed frame with a non-millisecond presentation time within the first half second. Cut exactly at that display timestamp, then 100 ns later. Compare the final source PTS retained by the production snapshot trim and every byte of its last decoded 48 by 32 RGB image with the original. Source reference uses the ordinary FFmpeg presentation clock in microseconds. Also record the independently demuxed timestamps of the stored frames.
picture_limitation: Matroska stores media packets on a millisecond grid. The exported PTS can differ from the original even when the final image and the separately recorded source timestamp are correct. The observed maximum difference was 495 microseconds.
